attachments.origin_landmark: adjacent metacarpal shafts (each with 2 heads, bipennate)
attachments.insertion_landmark: extensor expansion + proximal phalanx base, digits 2 (both sides), 3, 4

actions: abduct fingers away from the axial line (digit 3); assist MCP flexion/IP extension

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: 4 separate small bipennate muscles (TA: interossei dorsales I-IV) modeled here as one collective entity; each originates from 2 adjacent metacarpal shafts, a genuinely bipennate architecture.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the dorsum of the hand, 1-2 cm proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints; or longitudinally along the palpable metacarpal shafts.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Four muscles lying between the metacarpal cortices I-V.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Spasticity here can subluxate the proximal phalanx anteriorly and flex the metacarpophalangeal joint past 90 degrees. A 2023 study supported the in-plane longitudinal dorsal approach as safe and effective.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107
